Subject: Optimize Toolkit — scenario sheets & flexible pricing tiers

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I pulled together a couple of scenario sheets that show how batching, KV caching credits, and quantization options move the unit economics across your three usage patterns (search-heavy, chat augmentation, and nightly batch indexing).

Quick summary up front:
- Small pilot (0–100M tokens/month): best value is the "Pilot Flex" tier with modest caching credits and standard FP16 quantization — lowest up-front commit.
- Mid grow (100–500M tokens/month): "Commit Tier B" with 12-month commit yields ~22% effective token cost reduction when combined with 20% prefix caching.
- Scale (500M+): larger commit bands + aggressive int8 quantization and autoscale batching realize the largest savings but require a short performance QA window for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Actionable asks from you:
1) Which of the three patterns maps closest to your Week 1 usage profile? (search, chat, batch)
2) Are you open to a 12-month commit if we layer in an "ops buffer" — a small burst allowance you don't pay for until used?
3) Any compliance guards we should bake in (e.g., extra audit-log retention on Private deployments)?

Attached: RDW_Novum_pricing-scenarios_v1.xlsx (scenario tabs + token models) and a one-pager on the Optimize toolkit.

If it helps, I can run a quick baseline simulation for your NiceSearch index (you mentioned ~60M monthly tokens) — would you be able to share last month’s token distribution or a small sample query set?

Thanks,
Chloe

Chloe —

Putting together a concise reply to Evan's questions. Key points to include in our customer-facing note:
1) The 22% in the workbook assumes the 20% prefix cache hit you called out; I’ll mark the tab that shows both with/without cache so they can toggle.
2) Int8 quantization: typical p95 latency delta on Ampere V100-style instances is +10–25ms for short-chat (<128 tokens) after kernel tuning; for long-turns (>512 tokens) the delta shrinks and throughput improves. We should call out that we recommend a 2-week QA window with a canary rollout for chat endpoints.
3) 6-month commit: we can offer a "Short Commit" band that delivers ~12–15% savings vs retail and includes a smaller ops buffer. The trade is less favorable than 12-month; add-on caching credits can bridge ~4–6% if they agree to a modest usage profile share.

Pricing suggestion for the note:
- Pilot Flex (0–100M): no commit, 4% usage credit on KV caching, FP16 default.
- Short Commit (6m / 100–300M): ~13% off base, 8% caching credits, can include 5% one-time onboarding credit.
- Standard Commit (12m / 100–500M): ~22% off base, 20% caching credits, int8 advisory + 2-week QA window.

I’ll draft numbers into the spreadsheet and flag assumptions (token mix, sequence length distribution). Also recommend we include an example TCO line comparing their current cloud spend to a projected Redwood spend at 3 scale points.

-Marcus

Thanks for the quick reply and for looping Hannah in. Short answers up front and I attached an updated sheet with toggles so you can see cache/no-cache views.

- The 22% outcome is with a 20% prefix cache hit applied. I added a second column that shows the same band without cache so you can compare.
- Int8 p95 latency: conservative estimate +20ms for short chat turns. That is within our latency SLO for non-interactive paths; for interactive chat we recommend enabling int8 on background or noncritical routes first and running a 2-week canary to validate quality/latency. Marcus included the recommended canary checklist in the spreadsheet.
- 6-month commit: yes, we can do a Short Commit SKU. I attached a sample statement of work for a 6-month pilot that includes a 5% onboarding credit and a single mid-term reconciliation to rebalance credits if usage skews.

Next steps:
1) Hannah — could you share a last-30-day token distribution (CSV) or a small query sample? We’ll run the baseline sim and return a one-page TCO within 48 hours.
2) Evan — if 6 months feels right, we can draft a short contract and include the ops buffer clause; otherwise, I’ll prepare the 12-month arithmetic so you can compare.

We’re aiming to keep the commercial options flexible so you can ramp without surprise overages. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want Marcus to walk through the scenario toggles live.

Best,
Chloe
